part.text: {"variants":[{"id":"V1","title":"Ensemble size for rare extremes in the HENS SFNO large ensemble","text":"HENS ran 7,424 SFNO members per day for 92 summer-2023 dates and showed that huge ensembles sample 4-sigma tails and cut outliers, but it did not score top-percentile probabilities against ERA5. Run 1,000-member SFNO ensembles on a subset of those HENS dates, subsample 10-1,000 members, and score top-percentile wind, temperature and rainfall probabilities against ERA5 with fair CRPS and Brier scores. The open question is whether HENS's tail-sampling result turns into extreme-probability skill past the operational 50 members, or saturates because SFNO's members share error. If skill saturates, report the member count where it does.","root_link":"SAME: the director's C1 question made concrete on the model HENS used (SFNO), which the original idea cites only as prior context.","compute_open":"Ensemble members per forecast, about 10 to 1,000, on HENS's summer-2023 dates. Unknown: whether SFNO's extreme-probability skill saturates at the same member count as AIFS-ENS or keeps rising toward HENS's 7,424.","sequential":"not given","changes":"System studied: SFNO instead of AIFS-ENS. Answers HENS's unresolved question of whether its 7,424-member 4-sigma tail finding converts into ERA5-scored top-percentile probability skill and where that skill saturates."},{"id":"V2","title":"Ensemble size for rare extremes across a multi-season AIFS-ENS sample","text":"The original runs 7 dates x 1,000 members, so its rare-event scores rest on seven synoptic situations. Spend the same total, 7,500 member-runs, on 30 dates spread across seasons with 250 members each, then subsample 10-250 members and score top-percentile wind, temperature and rainfall probabilities against ERA5 and station observations with fair CRPS and Brier scores. The open question becomes whether the member-count conclusion holds across seasons and weather regimes, or whether the seven-date answer is regime-specific. Report the saturation member count per season.","root_link":"SAME: the director's C1 question, made concrete on a multi-season sample rather than seven dates.","compute_open":"Forecast dates and seasons, about 30, at 250 members. Unknown: whether the saturation member count is stable across seasons or regime-dependent.","sequential":"not given","changes":"Quantity more compute buys: synoptic-date and seasonal coverage at fixed member count, instead of members on seven dates. Closes the card's own 'applies to 7 dates; not a multi-season reforecast' gap, and its result is usable by ECMWF's operational AIFS-ENS verification."},{"id":"V3","title":"AIFS-ENS ensemble size judged against the operational physical ensemble","text":"Score AIFS-ENS not only against ERA5 reanalysis but against ECMWF's operational physical ensemble, IFS ENS, on the same dates, treating IFS ENS as the benchmark its 50 members must match. Run 1,000 AIFS-ENS v1 members for 7 dates, subsample 10-1,000, and compare top-percentile wind, temperature and rainfall probabilities from both ensembles with fair CRPS and Brier scores. The open question is whether adding AIFS-ENS members past 50 closes the gap to the physical ensemble's extreme probabilities, or whether shared ML model error leaves a floor IFS ENS does not have. Report the member count at which the gap stops shrinking.","root_link":"SAME: the director's C1 question, made concrete against the operational physical ensemble as the reference forecast.","compute_open":"Ensemble members per forecast, 10-1,000, plus paired IFS ENS members on the same dates. Unknown: whether the AIFS-ENS-to-IFS-ENS extreme-probability gap shrinks with more members or plateaus from shared ML error.","sequential":"not given","changes":"Comparison judged against: the operational ECMWF IFS ENS instead of ERA5 alone. Matters to ECMWF's operational ensemble design by asking whether member count can substitute for physical spread."}]}
